title: peatfire-eval: PeatFireBench and evaluation-protocol experiments for district-month fire severity forecasting in Indonesia
description:
Version 2.0.0 adds PeatFireBench, a district-month benchmark for fire forecasting in Indonesia: 498 districts and cities, 2012-2025, VIIRS S-NPP active fire detections with ENSO and IOD indices, CHIRPS rainfall, land cover, forest loss, terrain and population; eight baselines; chronological, extreme-year and island-transfer splits; two severity targets. The raw district-month panel and the per-district covariate tables are included; the full feature panel is rebuilt by the included scripts in seconds and is byte-identical to the one used in the accompanying article.

Code and derived data accompanying the manuscript Evaluation choices decide fire-prediction model rankings and whether they transfer between provinces: evidence from Indonesian Kalimantan.

Builds district-month panels of VIIRS S-NPP active fire detections for the 14 districts of West Kalimantan and the 55 districts of Indonesian Kalimantan, using GADM 4.1 administrative boundaries rather than a bounding box, and evaluates seven forecasting models under a 2x2 design crossing the test distribution (balanced or natural prevalence) with the discrimination metric (ROC-AUC or AUC-PR). Includes severity-threshold sensitivity, isotonic calibration fitted on out-of-fold predictions, bootstrap and per-year intervals, pooled and per-district severity targets, a negative result for the Indian Ocean Dipole, leave-one-province-out transfer, training-scope and province-identity tests, and a sensitivity analysis with thresholds computed from training years only.

Version 1.3.0 corrects the ONI timing: earlier versions assigned each three-month ONI season to its central month, so the lag-1 value included the target month. Seasons are now assigned to their last month. All results change slightly and supersede those of 1.0.0-1.2.0. 1.3.0 also adds decision-level analyses and robustness checks (kalimantan_keputusan.py, kalimantan_uji_tajam.py).

The derived panels (2,464 and 9,240 district-months) are included. Raw FIRMS detections and GADM boundaries are not redistributed; both are free to obtain and the README documents how.
